title: Add Dedicated rollout plan model + DB migrations
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Motivation: Dedicated customers and operators need a deterministic, auditable staged rollout mechanism for reserved pools (model versions, runtime builds, routing policy/config). This PR introduces the control-plane persistence model and migrations for DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan, including stage definitions and state machine fields, plus a small backfill to create a default “implicit plan” record for existing pools (so downstream APIs can treat the relationship as non-null).

Scope (DB + model only; no routing/policy behavior changes in this PR):
- New tables:
  - dedicated_pool_rollout_plans: top-level rollout plan object (pool-scoped) + current execution state
  - dedicated_pool_rollout_plan_stages: stage definitions (ordered), including traffic partition shape and optional gate policy reference
  - dedicated_pool_rollout_executions: execution instance fields (current stage index, timestamps, abort reason, etc.) to support future history/archival without rewriting plan rows
- State machine fields aligned with the rollout threads/ADR direction: DRAFT -> RUNNING -> (HELD|ABORTED|COMPLETED). Note: execution-level state is stored on dedicated_pool_rollout_executions; plan remains editable only while DRAFT.
- Stage definition supports two partition modes (per ADR draft):
  - PERCENT: split by requested traffic percent per stage
  - REPLICA_PARTITION: split by fixed replica allocations per stage (for small pools / deterministic capacity)
  For this PR we store both shapes in a constrained schema: stage_type + numeric fields + validation hooks in the model layer.
- Backfill/migration:
  - Adds rollout_plan_id nullable column to dedicated_pools with a follow-up backfill that creates an implicit plan per pool and sets rollout_plan_id.
  - The implicit plan is created as DRAFT with a single stage of 100% to “current” (no change) and a null gate policy.

Implementation details:
- Uses pg enums for execution_state and stage_type.
- Adds indexes for common access paths:
  - dedicated_pool_rollout_plans(pool_id) unique
  - dedicated_pool_rollout_plan_stages(plan_id, ordinal) unique
  - dedicated_pool_rollout_executions(plan_id, created_at desc)
- Adds optimistic concurrency fields on executions (version bigint) to support idempotent promote/abort in follow-up PRs.

Rollout / risk:
- Migration is additive and should be safe to deploy ahead of any feature flag enablement.
- Backfill is idempotent and chunked (batch size 500) to avoid long locks.
- No API surface change in this PR.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for model validations (stage ordinal uniqueness, partition bounds, enum state transitions).
- Migration tests on a snapshot with ~5k dedicated_pools.

Follow-ups:
- CRUD APIs + validation rules (ENG-5932) will build on this schema.
- Audit events for promote/abort will be introduced when execution actions land.

Refs:
- Customer escalation: SUP-28491 (phased upgrades request)
- Slack threads: state machine + idempotency discussions (eng-platform)
- ADRs in progress: stage model + rollback semantics (links in internal doc)

Checklist:
- [x] Migrations are backward compatible
- [x] Backfill is chunked + idempotent
- [x] Added indexes for expected query patterns
- [x] Added unit tests for model validations
- [x] Verified migration time on staging snapshot

conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we avoid pg enums here? They’re hard to evolve. Also: why separate executions table vs fields on plan?

Benji Okafor (author): Re enums: agree they’re annoying, but we want strictness for state machine + stage type. I can switch to text + CHECK constraints if you feel strongly. Re executions: the intent is to keep plan definition stable and allow multiple attempts / history later (and keep ABORT/COMPLETE timestamps from being overwritten if we restart).
Jordan Lee (review): +1 on execution separation. For enums: I’d prefer CHECK constraints so we can add new states without ALTER TYPE in prod.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated to text + CHECK constraints for execution_state and stage_type. Kept model-level enum wrapper so app code remains typed.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Backfill batch size 500 feels high if pools are hot; can we rate limit and ensure we don’t lock dedicated_pools too long?
Benji Okafor (author): Dropped to 200 and changed to update-by-primary-key in small transactions. Added sleep jitter between batches and a ‘max_runtime_minutes’ guard for safety.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add an explicit field for abort_reason / hold_reason with operator-provided text, we’ll need it for oncall + audit later.
Benji Okafor (author): Added nullable execution.abort_reason and execution.hold_reason (text). Not wired anywhere yet, but persisted for follow-up action endpoints.
Irene Choi (review): For replica partitions, we’ll need to enforce minimum replicas per stage to avoid fragmentation. Are we encoding that here?

Benji Okafor (author): Not enforcing infra headroom rules in DB layer yet. This PR adds ‘replica_count’ fields with >=0 constraint; infra-specific validation will live in the control-plane service validation in the CRUD PR (and should reference fleet signals). Added a TODO comment + test stub to make sure we don’t forget.
Ethan Park (review): Looks good after the CHECK constraint change. Please add an index for (plan_id, created_at desc) on executions for the “latest execution” query.
Benji Okafor (author): Added index dedicated_pool_rollout_executions_plan_id_created_at_idx and updated query helper accordingly.
Jordan Lee (approval): Approved. This is a good base for deterministic promote/abort with optimistic concurrency.
Ethan Park (approval): Approved. Please coordinate migration timing with release train once the feature flag work is ready.
release_notes: Internal: Adds persistence model + migrations for Dedicated staged rollout plans (no behavior change).
